## Natural history notes

A medium-sized flower fly characterized by its bee-like body, large eyes, dark abdomen with pale bands, and fuzzy yellowish to brown hairs that give it a plush-backed appearance. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, roadsides, wetlands, forest edges, parks, and other sunny habitats with abundant flowers and moist organic material nearby. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen and can act as pollinators, while the aquatic or semi-aquatic larvae develop in wet, decaying organic matter where they help break down nutrient-rich material.
